# `<` — Sort up / Less

Function. Hanzi: `小`. Ranks: `∞` monadic, `0 0` dyadic

`<Y` sorts the major cells of `Y` ascending, as `[⍋Y]⌷Y` does. Ties keep their order.

```bpl
<30 10 20           ⍝ 10 20 30
<"banana"           ⍝ "aaabnn"
<[3 1⋄1 2⋄2 0]  ⍝ [1 2⋄2 0⋄3 1]
```

`X<Y` tests X < Y for reals. Pervasive; tolerant.

```bpl
1 2 3<2            ⍝ $t $f $f
```

See [`>`](greater-than.qmd) to sort down, and [`⍋`](delta-stile.qmd) for the indices that sort.

## Fast combinations

These trains and compositions give the result of applying their parts in turn, faster. [Trains](../evaluation.qmd#trains) says which spellings BPL recognises.

| Combination | Applies to | Benefit |
|---|---|---|
| `k↑< Y` or `(k↑)∘<` | a vector of reals or characters without keys, with the count at most a quarter of its length | selects the `k` smallest items, or the `-k` largest, without ordering the rest |
| `↑< Y`, `i⌷< Y` or `i⊃< Y` | the same vectors | selects the item of rank `i`, such as a median, without ordering the rest |

```bpl
v←30 10 20 50 40 60 70 80 90 0
2↑< v                                ⍝ 0 10
5⌷< v                                ⍝ 50
(•explain "5⌷< v").fast.combination  ⍝ ["partial sort"]
```
